│ docs are load-bearing and mostly verifiable from the tree, the process records (decision log,  │
│ changelog, growth accounting) are the best I have read, and the guardrail system even tests    │
│ itself. The one material contradiction is size: four crates sit far above the line budgets     │
│ docs/ARCHITECTURE.md publishes for them, with yi-runtime at 7.6× its ceiling.                  │
│ What it is                                                                                     │
│ Yi is a personal coding agent in native Rust, at version 0.309.0, in active daily development  │
│ (the changelog's top five rows are dated today, 2026-09-24). Fifteen crates, one 5.7 MB        │
│ binary, 20 direct dependencies, plus a kernel-side Python package (python/yi_runtime) for the  │
│ Jupyter runtime and subagents. The design is a pure turn loop (yi-loop, 1,340 src lines)       │
│ emitting one 13-variant event enum, with every surface — CLI, TUI, workspace console, ACP      │
│ editor protocol, daemon — a client rendering the same stream (README "Architecture",           │
│ YI_DESIGN.md §2).                                                                              │
│ Findings, the contradictions first                                                             │
│ 1. Crate line budgets are stated and exceeded. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md publishes per-crate        │
│    budgets as ceilings ("the target is always smaller"): yi-runtime 6,000, yi-tools 9,000,     │
│    yi-tui 9,406, yi-cli 2,000. Measured now with find crates/*/src -name '*.rs' | xargs wc -l: │
│    runtime 45,905, tools 12,412, tui 12,657, cli 4,556. Runtime is 7.6× its published ceiling. │
│    Either the budget figure means something else than source lines (the doc does not say) or   │
│    the ratchet stopped being repriced and the doc is stale. Either way the map and the tree    │
│    disagree, and this is the repo's own doctrine: the feature ledger claims budgets are        │
│    "enforced by CI, not by intention".                                                         │
│ 2. Unwraps exist in production paths by naive count. grep -rn '\.unwrap()' crates/*/src        │
│    --include='*.rs' | wc -l = 80, plus 7 .expect(, 0 panic!, 0 non-comment unsafe (the single  │
│    grep hit for "unsafe" is a comment at [MASKED]). Concentrations:                            │
│    runtime/src/memory/store.rs 28, oauth/src/store.rs 15, runtime/src/memory/doc.rs 11. The    │
│    repository's rule is "no unwrap/expect outside tests" (README Contribute), and a dedicated  │
│    gate ([MASKED]) runs in just check, so most of these are almost certainly inside inline     │
│    #[cfg(test)] modules my line-wise grep cannot exclude; I did not read all 80 sites, so this │
│    is a count with that caveat, not a finding of rule-breaking.                                │

│    rows run to thousands of characters (the 0.301.0 OAuth row alone is roughly 2,500           │
│    characters of prose). This is superb for archaeology and poor for a first read; the same    │
│    detail also lives in the decision log, so one of the two records could be the summary.      │

│ │                                      │       │ #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and module list,    │ │
│ │                                      │       │ the pure serde wall it claims to be. One    │ │
│ │                                      │       │ deduction: the runtime crate is a           │ │
│ │                                      │       │ 45.9k-line monolith holding subagents,      │ │
│ │                                      │       │ plans, goals, schedules, memory, advisor    │ │
│ │                                      │       │ and lanes in one dependency plane (the      │ │
│ │                                      │       │ design itself flagged this risk in §2 and   │ │
│ │                                      │       │ accepted it as modules).                    │ │

│ │                                      │       │ design, failures are stream values. Recent  │ │
│ │                                      │       │ history shows the review process catching   │ │
│ │                                      │       │ real concurrency defects (double-ending a   │ │

│ │                                      │       │ parallel, each with a --selfcheck proving   │ │

│ │                                      │       │ tiers in the justfile with a lane invariant │ │

│ │                                      │       │ weighed-and-rejected alternatives named.    │ │
│ │                                      │       │ The four-tier structure (pre-commit / push  │ │

│ │                                      │       │ startup are ratcheted, dependencies are     │ │

│ │                                      │       │ the 0.259→0.309 stack added +14,940 src     │ │
